title.narrative: BVLF - Jordan 2025-2026 - First Steps Big Step 3 ECD

description.narrative:
Implementing partners: -PLAN INTERNATIONAL JORDAN (PIJO) role: Coordination between partners/stakeholders, partners’ capacity strengthening, advocating for ECD as a national priority with other stakeholders, bringing in regional/ global ECD knowledge and experience, Project management, PMEL, quality assurance throughout the project implementation; Child Safeguarding and Gender Equality. -ROYAL HEALTH AWARENESS SOCIETY (RHAS) role: Conduct parenting training program for 45 MoH core team members by delivering inclusive parenting content to health workers and parents, rolling out inclusive parenting training delivery, strengthening referral pathways, coordinating with other service providers/partners on parenting and working with MoH on institutionalized mechanisms to promote ECD.
Key Stakeholders: -Ministry of Health (MoH) role: taking ownership of the project and build their staff’s capacity on ECD through focal points, facilitating coordination with stakeholders and staff, supervising and delivering parenting sessions, quality control of facilitators’ performance, community awareness. Furthermore, MoH will work with FSBS-3 partners on institutionalizing ECD within MoH policies, budgets, programmes and developing and endorsing ECD standards. -THE HEALTH CARE ACCREDITATION COUNCIL (HCAC) role: executing the FSBS-2 developed ECD standards and establish a National Recognition System, delivering initial quality assessments, mock surveys and final evaluations at selected MoH centres, awarding accreditation to health centres fulfilling the required quality standards; capacity building of health workers; providing consultation services to support change; supporting government in realizing their potential to steer healthcare improvement; enhancing performance related to governance, standards, accreditation, and capacity building; providing policy reform advice and enhancing engagement and awareness. - National Center for Family Affairs: provide technical support to the ECD national committee and the consortium members.
The proposed consortium is a trusted and experienced partnership between Plan International Jordan, RHAS, HCAC, MoH, NCFA), Their combined experience provides a solid foundation for delivering the project objectives efficiently and at scale

Jordan continues to face significant challenges in delivering equitable and high-quality Early Childhood Development (ECD) services, particularly for children and caregivers from socially and economically disadvantaged backgrounds. While recent efforts have led to some progress, many families in underserved areas—especially in the southern governorates—still lack access to essential health, education, and developmental support.
Persistent regional instability and an overstretched public healthcare system have further disrupted consistent service delivery. This has resulted in missed opportunities for early detection of developmental issues, timely interventions, and meaningful parental engagement.
These gaps disproportionately affect mothers, limiting their ability to participate in the labor market, pursue education, and advance socially and professionally. As a result, households face increased economic pressure, reinforcing gender inequities and marginalize women from an inclusive participation in decision-making processes.

Key activities include expanding services to 20 new health centers, especially in underserved areas, and providing technical support to sustain previous initiatives. The project will train 45 new trainers and community health practitioners in parenting programs, emphasizing gender equality and male engagement, as well as training 40 MoH staff to deliver these programs in targeted health centers. To support program expansion, three out of the participating centers will be selected to facilitate training integration into MoH professional development and will be recognized as Centers of Excellence.
These selected Centers of Excellence are expected to play a key role in scaling up the parenting empowerment program. Their functions will include aligning program implementation with HCAC quality standards, promoting inclusive practices, and enhancing the program’s sustainability. These centers will also serve as hubs for capacity building by implementing twinning and shadowing arrangements with at least two additional health centers. To effectively fulfill this role, the centers will require investment in qualified staff, continuous training, and adequate infrastructure and resources. Standardization and Quality Recognition System of ECD services will be implemented in selected centers, complemented by strengthened community outreach via mobile apps, social media, and local activities. Public-private partnerships will be fostered to fund and promote ECD initiatives, while advocacy efforts will leverage the recent social behavior change study findings to promote robust ECD policies within the health system.

SUMMARY First Steps’ Big Step (FSBS) Phase 3 is a two-years extension for the project funded by the Bernard van Leer Foundation and Plan International Netherlands and designed to empower parents through community-based approaches, by teaching them how to create a more enabling home environment to better respond to children’s needs without gender discrimination or violence. Parenting programmes have been implemented to bolster gender-transformative thinking and psychosocial support. FSBS-2 will establish an evidence-based strategy to assure adequate interventions, Evidence that has been derived from FSBS-1 project, will be utilized to reinforce and shape the future activities as well. For example, the FSBS-2 project will utilize the male engagement findings to provide suggestions for exploring new techniques to execute the various interventions around male engagement, as well as to use the findings at policy level to establish policy that supports men in engaging with their children. This project will strengthen the MoH’s capacity to deliver accessible, high-quality, and standardized ECD services. This includes expanding infrastructure, training health practitioners, and fostering collaborations with key partners. By doing so, the project seeks to ensure early developmental support reaches children in the most disadvantaged communities, reducing disparities, promoting inclusive growth, and laying a foundation for a healthier, more equitable future for Jordan’s children. The primary objective of this investment is to institutionalize inclusive, high-quality ECD services within Jordan’s health system by strengthening MoH’s capacity, expanding sustainable parenting programs, and enhancing national coordination mechanisms. FSBS-3 aims to scale up gender-responsive, evidence-based ECD interventions, embed them in national policies and professional development frameworks, and establish public-private partnerships for long-term sustainability. Through strengthened service delivery, digital innovation, and policy advocacy, the project will ensure that all children, including those with disabilities, receive nurturing care and developmental support from birth, particularly in underserved regions.
